Build a dependency graph from a library or lockfile

Source: R/build_dep_graph.R
build_dep_graph.Rd

Constructs a directed igraph dependency graph where an edge A -> B means "package A requires package B". Vertices carry the package version, source and whether the package is actually present in the scanned set, so that missing dependencies show up as vertices with present = FALSE. The returned object also gains the class bw_depgraph for a richer print method, while remaining a fully functional igraph object.

Usage

build_dep_graph(x, include_base = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A bw_library (from scan_library()), or a path that scan_library() understands.

include_base

Logical; include edges to base/recommended packages that ship with R. Defaults to FALSE to keep the DAG focused on the distribution under management.

Value

An igraph object of class bw_depgraph. Vertex attributes: version, source, present, is_base. Edge attribute: constraint (the raw requirement string, e.g. ">= 1.0.0" or "").

See also

bw_cycles(), bw_diamonds(), detect_conflicts()

Examples

g <- build_dep_graph(bw_example("clean.lock"))
g
#> 
#> ── buildwright dependency graph ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 14 packages, 23 dependency edges
#> 14 present / 0 referenced-but-missing
#> ✔ Acyclic (a valid install order exists)
#> 6 shared (diamond) dependencies
igraph::vcount(g)
#> [1] 14
bw_cycles(g)
#> list()
